messages:
Alex Chen: quick update — ran RoPE-scaling matrix across Mixtral / Mistral / Qwen with linear, NTK and YARN variants. seeing a clear divergence in long-context behavior + perf for Mixtral.
Priya Patel: pls paste the numbers when you have them. what hardware? :eyes:
Alex Chen: tests on p4d. baseline (no scaling) vs variants at 2k/8k/32k contexts. short summary:
```
Mixtral: linear ok to ~8k, NTK shows perplexity spike after 8k (x1.4 @32k), YARN stabilizes quality but increases CPU by ~12%.
Mistral: linear + YARN both stable to 16k, NTK slightly better perplexity at 32k but higher memory churn.
Qwen: NTK is required beyond 16k, linear breaks earlier (loss drift).
```
Samir Dutta: interesting — what about runtime perf (tokens/sec) and kernels chosen?
Alex Chen: right — profiling shows kernel selection flips at long seqs. fused-causal-attn becomes inefficient for Mixtral shapes and we fall back to a multi-head kernel that increases launch overhead.
- kernel selection: fused->fallback around seq_len 10k for Mixtral.
- batching heuristics: our continuous-batching keeps joining small requests which helps throughput but causes longer-lived KV objects and occasional eviction when KV memory pressure rises.
- KV cache: Mixtral implementation appended RoPE scaling state into cache key; that increased cache misses after switching variants (cache_miss_rate 0.12 -> 0.45 in some runs).
Mei Wong: can you share the profiler traces? low-level numbers (SM occupancy, kernel time) would help.
Alex Chen: pasted a tiny snippet (trimmed):
```
Mixtral @32k, YARN: attention kernel 1: 43ms, kernel 2: 12ms, memcpy: 18ms, SM occ: 62%
Mixtral @32k, NTK: attention kernel 1: 58ms, kernel 2: 8ms, SM occ: 48%  // more stalls
```
eng-bench-bot: benchmark run 1752461823 finished: 1200 iters, aggregated p50/p95 tokens/sec attached.
Priya Patel: so two problems: quality regressions (perplexity spike) and perf regressions (kernel fallback + KV churn). any suspected commit/regression?
Alex Chen: candidate: earlier change to RoPE state encoding (commit abc123) changed how we tag cache entries + a runtime heuristic tweak that prefers kernel fallback at seq>8k. both together explain mismatch.
Samir Dutta: plan: 1) revert RoPE state encoding and re-run microbench; 2) force fused kernel on Mixtral shape to measure delta; 3) add a KV cache-tag compatibility flag for rollout.
Mei Wong: agree. also can we add a per-model safe-range config to the routing layer so we don't route long-context Mixtral to hosted pool until we validate? helps dedicated customers.
Alex Chen: yep — provisional safe ranges from these runs:
- Mixtral: safe <= 8k for linear/NTK? YARN ok to 32k for quality but pay CPU.
- Mistral: safe <= 16k for linear, NTK optional.
- Qwen: prefer NTK past 16k; linear not safe beyond 8-12k depending on head dim.
Priya Patel: SGTM. Samir can you take the revert + forced-kernel experiments today? I can own the KV-tag rollback and add compatibility flag.
Samir Dutta: will run kernel-forcing microbenchmarks now. posting initial results in ~20m.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for kv-tag-compatibility flag (rollout: 10%).
Alex Chen: thanks — once we have microbench numbers we should publish a short doc for ops + routing that lists per-model safe ranges and known tradeoffs (cost vs quality) so customers know what to expect.
Mei Wong: also add an entry for batching heuristic — maybe cap continuous-batching window for long-context models to avoid KV pressure.
Samir Dutta: initial microbench: forcing fused kernel improves tokens/sec by ~22% at 32k for Mixtral, but memory usage up ~8%.
Priya Patel: perfect. next actions: Samir (kernel microbench + raw traces), Priya (kv-tag rollback PR + rollout), Alex (write ops doc draft), Mei (routing safe-range PR). :thumbsup:
Alex Chen: I'll drop the ops doc draft here when ready. thanks everyone.
